title: Transfer from a generic rank-one witness to integral ideal pushforwards
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] from an integral scheme $Z$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-weil-irreducible-components], and put $T=i(Z)$ and $\xi=i(\eta)$. For a module $F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] put $\operatorname{Supp}(F)=\{x\in X:F_x\ne0\}$, with module stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $\mathcal P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] supported in $T$. Suppose $\mathcal P(0)$; suppose that in every short exact sequence of coherent modules supported in $T$, if two terms have $\mathcal P$ then so does the third; and suppose that every coherent $Q$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(Q)\subseteq T$ and $Q_\xi=0$ has $\mathcal P$. Suppose there is a coherent module $G$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(G)=T$ and $\mathcal P(G)$ such that its stalk $G_\xi$ is killed by the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_\xi\subseteq\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ and is one-dimensional over the residue field $\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field], with scalar multiplication induced by $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}\to\kappa(\xi)$. Then for every quasi-coherent ideal $J\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, including $J=0$, $\mathcal P(i_*J)$ holds, where $i_*$ is module pushforward [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: For any quasi-coherent ideal $L\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, the coherent pushforward ideal lemma gives coherence of $i_*L$, since $X$ is locally Noetherian, $i$ is closed, and $Z$ is integral. Closed-pushforward stalks vanish outside $T=i(Z)$, so $\operatorname{Supp}(i_*L)\subseteq T$. If $J=0$, the sectionwise formula $(i_*0)(V)=0(i^{-1}V)=0$ identifies $i_*0$ with zero, and isomorphism invariance and $\mathcal P(0)$ give the conclusion. Henceforth take $J\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 01YH, label lemma-property-irreducible, third and fourth proof paragraphs

proof.text: Apply the rank-one generic ideal inclusion lemma to the given $G$. Its hypotheses are exactly the Noetherian condition, the integral closed immersion, coherence of $G$, and the scalar-compatible residue-field line at $\xi$. It gives a nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ and a monomorphism $\alpha:i_*I\to G$ with $\alpha_\xi$ an isomorphism. Let $Q=\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha)$. Coherent kernel/cokernel closure makes $Q$ coherent. Stalk exactness gives $Q_x=G_x/\alpha_x((i_*I)_x)$, so $Q_\xi=0$, and $Q_x=0$ outside $T$ because $G_x=0$ there. Thus $\mathcal P(Q)$ by the small-support hypothesis. In the short exact sequence $0\to i_*I\xrightarrow{\alpha}G\to Q\to0$, all terms are coherent and supported in $T$ by step 1 and the hypotheses. Since $\mathcal P(G)$ and $\mathcal P(Q)$ hold, two out of three gives $\mathcal P(i_*I)$.

source.place: Tag 01YH, label lemma-property-irreducible, third and fourth proof paragraphs

proof.text: The isomorphism $\alpha_\xi$ to the one-dimensional nonzero stalk $G_\xi$ shows that $i_*I$ is nonzero. Apply the common generic lattice lemma to $I$ and the nonzero ideal $J$. It yields a coherent module $K$ and monomorphisms $d:K\to i_*I$ and $b:K\to i_*J$, both isomorphisms at $\xi$. Put $Q_I=\operatorname{Coker}(d)$ and $Q_J=\operatorname{Coker}(b)$. Step 1 supplies coherence of both ideal pushforwards, so coherent kernel/cokernel closure makes $Q_I,Q_J$ coherent. By stalk exactness, $K_x$ injects into $(i_*I)_x=0$ when $x\notin T$, hence $K_x=0$ there. Likewise $(Q_I)_x$ and $(Q_J)_x$ are quotients of zero outside $T$, while $(Q_I)_\xi=(Q_J)_\xi=0$ because $d_\xi,b_\xi$ are isomorphisms. Consequently $K,Q_I,Q_J$ are all supported in $T$, and the hypothesis gives $\mathcal P(Q_I)$ and $\mathcal P(Q_J)$.

source.place: Tag 01YH, label lemma-property-irreducible, third and fourth proof paragraphs

proof.text: Use two out of three on $0\to K\xrightarrow{d}i_*I\to Q_I\to0$. Step 2 gives $\mathcal P(i_*I)$ and step 3 gives $\mathcal P(Q_I)$, hence $\mathcal P(K)$. Then use it on $0\to K\xrightarrow{b}i_*J\to Q_J\to0$ to obtain $\mathcal P(i_*J)$ from $\mathcal P(K)$ and $\mathcal P(Q_J)$. Steps 1 and 3 verified coherence and support for every term, so both applications are within the stated domain of $\mathcal P$. Together with the zero-ideal case this proves the assertion for every $J$.
